text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition parties contesting the November 18 general elections have accused former president Kenneth Kaunda of trying to usurp power by appointing himself their spokesman. They were responding to criticism by the former president, who said they should have boycotted the elections as his party has done.

- Zambia is one of six countries that will be involved in discussions on the development of the Beira Corridor to expand industry, commerce, agriculture and mining in the sub-region. The meeting will be held in Harare on December 2 to 3.

- Copperbelt Province police chief Alexander Makayi said the force would arrest people who were collecting voter cards to prevent people from voting in elections set for November 18. Former president Kenneth Kaunda, whose party is boycotting the elections, is leading a 'don't-vote' campaign and has instructed his officials to persuade intending voters to hand over their cards to the party.

- Cotton production in Zambia is poised for a major boost following the formation of Cotmark Company to promote cotton growing. Former workers of the state-run Lint Company of Zambia (Linto) have pooled resources to form the company.
